cards.text: Moses is still preaching to Israel about how to live and worship in the land God is giving them. Now he warns them about one kind of person. Say a prophet or dreamer of dreams arises among them and proclaims a sign or wonder.

cards.question: True or false: in Moses' example, the prophet's sign or wonder actually comes about.
The prophet's sign or wonder comes about. Then what does he tell Israel to do?

answers.text: Follow other gods and worship them
Build an altar on every hill

cards.text: So the man CALLS HIS SHOT, friend. At the end on that counter, I couldn't even call where my own stamp was gonna land!

cards.question: The prophet's sign came true, but he's pushing other gods. What does Moses say Israel must do?
Moses says the LORD your God is ___ you, to find out whether you love Him with all your heart and all your soul.

cards.text: Testing, friend. Like a cookie in the oven, you find out what it's really made of when the heat comes on.

cards.question: Instead of following other gods, who does Moses say Israel is to follow?

cards.text: Then Moses piles it on: fear Him, keep His commandments, listen to His voice, serve Him and hold fast to Him. Six verbs in one verse, and NOT ONE of them is maybe.
Then it gets serious. Moses says that prophet or dreamer must be put to death.

cards.question: Why does Moses say the false prophet or dreamer must be put to death?

answers.text: He advocated rebellion against the LORD
He lied about the sign he gave
He claimed to be Israel's king

cards.question: True or false: Moses describes the LORD the prophet rebels against as the One who brought Israel out of Egypt and redeemed them from the house of slavery.

cards.text: And Moses lands it like this: "So you must purge the evil from among you."
Now Moses brings it closer to home. WAY closer.

cards.question: This time, who does Moses picture trying to pull someone toward other gods?

answers.text: Their own family or closest friend
A traveler from a far land
A priest serving at the altar

cards.question: True or false: Moses says this family member or friend tries to pull them in openly, in front of everyone.

cards.text: Secretly, friend. And the gods on offer could belong to the peoples near or far, from one end of the earth to the other.

cards.question: When someone that close secretly pushes other gods, what does Moses say to do?

answers.text: Do not yield or listen to him
Talk it over with the family

cards.text: And Moses doesn't soften it: show him no pity, don't spare him, don't shield him. That's your brother, your kid, the person you'd hand your last cookie to.

cards.question: In this case, whose hand does Moses say must be first against the one who enticed?

cards.text: Then come the hands of all the people, and he is stoned for trying to turn them away from the LORD. Moses names Him again as the God who brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

cards.question: Moses says then all Israel will hear and be ___, and will never again do such a wicked thing among them.

cards.text: Now Moses zooms out from one house to a whole city. Say word comes that wicked men in one of Israel's cities have led their people astray, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods".

cards.question: When Israel hears that report about one of their cities, what does Moses say to do first?

answers.text: Send a prophet to warn it

cards.text: Inquire, investigate, interrogate. That's the OPPOSITE of the group chat, where one screenshot and everybody's already mad.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says Israel acts only if it is established with certainty that this abomination happened.

cards.text: Once it's certain, the judgment is total. The inhabitants are put to the sword, and all its people and livestock are devoted to destruction.

cards.question: Israel gathers all the city's plunder in the middle of the public square. Then what does Moses say they do with it?

answers.text: Burn it along with the city

cards.question: True or false: Moses says the burned city may be rebuilt someday.

cards.text: Nothing devoted to destruction shall cling to their hands, Moses says. Not one souvenir, not even a crumb.

cards.question: If Israel keeps none of the devoted things, what does Moses say the LORD will turn from?
Moses says the LORD will grant mercy, show compassion and ___ them, as He swore to their fathers.
True or false: Moses says this mercy comes because Israel obeys the LORD, keeps all His commandments and does what is right in His eyes.

cards.text: That's where we'll set this batch down for now. But Moses is NOT done preaching, friend. Not even close.

findings.problem: Moses is the first person to show up in the lesson, but the card never says who he is. It just says "Moses is still preaching to Israel."

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This card is only a reaction to the sign coming true, which card 2 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage, but it cites 13:2 anyway.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. "At the end on that counter" is unclear wording. Missing where a stamp lands is also a different action from calling a sign before it happens, so the comparison doesn't match the core action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This card repeats "Testing," the answer from card 6, and adds a cookie comparison. It tells no new part of the passage, so it works as a recap card.
The right answer uses the formal BSB word "advocated." The two wrong answers use plain everyday wording, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question asks whose hand must be "first against" the one who enticed. No earlier card says he is to be put to death (13:9 "you must surely kill him"), so the question doesn't say first against him for what.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never says that the city and its plunder are burned "as a whole burnt offering to the LORD your God" (13:16). That is the detail that explains why everything is burned.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question says the LORD rewards obedience. In that setting, turning from "His promise to their fathers" or "His chosen dwelling place" isn't believable as a reward, so only "His fierce anger" makes sense.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: The blank sits in a list of mercies ("grant mercy, show compassion and ___ them"). "Scatter" and "judge" are the opposite of mercy, so the baker can rule them out at once and the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
